context:
Treat this as connector compatibility hardening, not a broad Trino adapter
refactor. First prove whether Trino still rejects PRIMARY KEY metadata in the
relevant connector modes. Only then mirror the narrow Presto helper ordering.
description:
The JoinOrder Presto DDL remediation added `strip_primary_keys()` to
`PrestoAdapter._optimize_table_definition()` after Presto rejected benchmark
CREATE TABLE statements that carried PRIMARY KEY metadata. Trino has a
parallel `_optimize_table_definition()` path and currently does not call the
shared helper. If Trino becomes a canonical JoinOrder target, the same DDL
failure shape may recur.

This is not release-blocking for the JoinOrder remediation batch because the
reviewed target was Presto, not Trino. Keep it as a scoped follow-up unless a
Trino JoinOrder UAT failure makes it urgent.

anti_patterns.dont: factor Presto and Trino DDL optimization into a new shared abstraction unless multiple non-PK rewrites also converge
run live Trino/cloud tests without explicit approval
use broad regex rewrites in the adapter when `strip_primary_keys()` already handles nested parentheses

preserves.behavior: Do not change the canonical JoinOrder schema, query set, row counts, or reference cardinalities
Do not remove FOREIGN KEY metadata unless a Trino-specific failure proves it is necessary
Keep SDK imports lazy and do not require a live Trino server for unit coverage

tests/unit/platforms/test_presto_adapter.py: focused adapter optimizer coverage without a live server
